title: Source transition under a thickening
statement: Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative ring, $q\in\mathbf Z$, $p:X\to S$ and $g:T_2\to S$ morphisms of schemes [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], and $i:T_1\to T_2$ a closed immersion surjective on points. For every etale sheaf $F$ of $\Lambda$-modules on $T_2$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves], the canonical restriction transition between the sources of [sbc-def-base-change-map], $p^{-1}R^qg_*F\to p^{-1}R^q(g i)_*i^{-1}F$, is an isomorphism.

source.place: Proof, condition (1): thickenings; transition compatibility made explicit

proof.text: By [sbc-lem-thickening-etale-site], pullback along i is an equivalence. Deriving its adjunction gives an equivalence on bounded-below derived categories, so its unit is invertible. To see the derived equivalence directly, apply the additive equivalence and its exact inverse degreewise to bounded-below complexes: they preserve quasi-isomorphisms and their inverse natural isomorphisms descend to the localization.

The canonical transition is Rg_* applied to that unit followed by the composition isomorphism for direct images. Pull back along p, apply degree-q homology, and insert the isomorphism comparing the inverse image of a degree-zero complex with its pulled-back sheaf placed in degree zero. All factors are invertible. For the identification of the transition, use the composite-unit formula [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction] and the conjugate-defined right-adjoint comparison [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate]. Substitute these formulas; naturality moves the intervening counit past the unit, and the triangle identity cancels the unit-counit pair for g (respectively h2). The remaining map is the direct image of the invertible unit for i (respectively a).
